record.paper_title: Modal logics for metric spaces: open problems
record.original_question: Classify fragments of MS over different classes C of distance models according to their satisfiability and axiomatisation behavior. For each such class, are there natural maximal decidable fragments, and if so, what is the computational complexity of satisfiability for those fragments under unary and binary encodings of numerical parameters?

artifact.status_search_result: The broad classification problem for fragments of the modal language MS over various classes of distance and metric spaces, together with sharp complexity bounds under unary vs binary encoding of distance parameters and identification of maximal decidable fragments, remains an active research program. Partial results identify several decidable fragments and undecidability of full MS / the two-variable fragment of the associated first-order distance language over metric spaces (Kutz–Wolter–Zakharyaschev and related work), but a complete classification with maximal decidable fragments and tight complexity under both encodings has not been established.

status_evidence.title: Logics of metric spaces (Kutz, Wolter, Sturm, Zakharyaschev)
status_evidence.snippet: Introduces the modal distance language MS, shows undecidability of the full language and identifies several decidable fragments over classes of distance spaces with the triangle inequality and over metric spaces.
status_evidence.claim: The classification of MS fragments has only been partially completed; several decidable fragments are known, alongside undecidability of the full language.

status_evidence.title: From topology to metric: modal logic and quantification in metric spaces
status_evidence.snippet: Further studies of expressive modal languages over metric spaces, with decidability and complexity results for selected fragments.
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent work has extended the picture for specific fragments but has not produced an exhaustive classification with maximal decidable fragments and tight unary/binary complexity bounds.
